items.title: In-vitro exposure to mercury chloride, with and without n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, on the Th17-associated immune response in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from systemic lupus erythematosus patients.
items.abstract: T H 17 cytokines are implicated in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) pathogenesis. Mercury is an environmental factor associated with the exacerbation of SLE pathology, potentially by regulating the Th H 17 pathway. Humans are primarily exposed to mercury from dental amalgams and fish consumption. Fish are also a rich source of the n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and have been shown to reduce SLE disease symptoms. This pilot in-vitro investigation isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from SLE patients ( N  = 15) and healthy controls (HC, N  = 15). The cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and exposed to 200 nM of mercury (II) chloride (HgCl) for 24 hr, with or without pre-exposure (24 hr) to either EPA or DHA at 100 μM each. The T H 17-associated cytokines were quantified in the PBMC supernatants. Pre-exposure to EPA resulted in significantly lower concentrations of IL-27 in supernatants of LPS-HgCl treated PBMC from SLE patients (29.58 [± 22.62] pg/mL) compared to HCs (51.63 [± 42.96] pg/mL) ( p  = 0.04). While DHA-LPS-HgCl had significantly lower IL-27 concentrations compared in LPS-HgCl in PBMC from SLE patients and HCs, there was no significant difference between groups. IL-27 exhibits pro/anti-inflammatory effects on the immune system. We suggest that the observed reductions in IL-27 concentrations following EPA-LPS-HgCl treatment support the protective role of n-3 PUFA in autoimmune responses.

items.title: Genetic Prioritization of BTN3A2 Reveals an Interferon-Responsive T-Cell Program in Dermatomyositis Through Single-Cell Mendelian Randomization and Multi-Omics Integration.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by genetic susceptibility and dysregulated immune activation. However, the relationship between genetic variation and specific immune cell states remains poorly understood. We aimed to identify genetically supported immune-cell-specific molecular programs underlying DM and investigate their biological relevance. We integrated immune-cell-specific single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs) from the OneK1K cohort with DM genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Candidate genes were replicated using an independent sc-eQTL dataset and prioritized by Bayesian colocalization. Multi-tissue validation was performed using skeletal muscle transcriptomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and skin single-cell RNA sequencing, protein expression data, clinical phenotypes, virtual knockout analysis, and gain-of-function analyses of BTN3A2. We identified 204 immune cell-specific eGenes associated with DM and prioritized four high-confidence genes, including HLA-DRB1, HLA-C, Lnc-HLA-B-2, and BTN3A2. BTN3A2 showed robust colocalization across multiple CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell subsets and was further supported by muscle transcriptomic data. BTN3A2 was consistently upregulated in both DM muscle tissues and PBMCs and was broadly expressed across T-cell, NK-cell, and B-cell populations. BTN3A2 + T cells exhibited enhanced cytotoxic, activation, antigen-presentation, and interferon-responsive programs, which were reproduced in circulating PBMCs and lesional skin T cells. BTN3A2 expression was negatively correlated with MMT8 scores, while in silico knockout analysis implicated interferon-stimulated and antiviral pathways. Integrating cell-type-specific genetic evidence with multi-tissue immune profiling identified BTN3A2 as a genetically supported candidate associated with DM and an interferon-responsive T-cell state, providing novel insights for future mechanistic investigation.

items.title: Sustained Tocilizumab and Adjunctive HydroBox Therapy in Refractory Takayasu Arteritis: An 11-year Case Report.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TAK) is a rare, chronic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly affecting young women, characterized by progressive stenosis and occlusion of the aorta and its major branches. Despite advances in biologic therapy, refractory disease with recurrent vascular complications remains a significant clinical challenge. Molecular hydrogen-based adjuvant (HydroBox) therapy has emerged as a promising adjuvant approach owing to its antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties. This report aims to describe the long-term clinical course and therapeutic outcomes of a patient with refractory TAK managed with sustained tocilizumab and HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy over 11 years. We report the case of a 25-year-old female with refractory TAK first diagnosed at age 13, presenting with sudden vision loss, dizziness, and pulseless upper extremities. Disease course was complicated by extensive great-vessel involvement, multiple cerebral infarctions, and recurrent in-stent restenosis despite ongoing interleukin-6 (IL-6) blockade. Over 50 courses of tocilizumab (Actemra) were administered from 2014 onward, combined with multiple percutaneous transluminal angioplasty and stenting procedures. HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy was subsequently introduced as an adjunctive treatment. During continued follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable with sustained suppression of inflammatory markers and favorable cerebrovascular findings on serial imaging. This 11-year case report documents the feasibility of sustained long-term tocilizumab therapy combined with adjunctive HydroBox therapy in a patient with refractory TAK. Despite extensive multi-vessel involvement, recurrent in-stent restenosis, and prior cerebrovascular ischemia, the patient achieved progressive hemodynamic stabilization, durable suppression of inflammatory markers, and continued disease control. The potential immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties of HydroBox-assisted therapy warrant further prospective investigation to establish standardized protocols and confirm efficacy in larger cohorts.

items.title: In Vivo Dynamics of Immunoregulatory Lymphocyte Reconstitution: A Seven-year Longitudinal Study of Sustained Remission in Class IV Lupus Nephritis Following Rituximab Therapy.
items.abstract: Rituximab (RTX)-induced B-cell depletion is an established treatment for refractory lupus nephritis (LN). However, the in vivo kinetics of B-cell reconstitution and their association with sustained clinical remission remain poorly characterized. Because cluster of differentiation 19-positive (CD19 + ) B-cell monitoring provides a practical measure of immune reconstitution after RTX therapy, we investigated the longitudinal in vivo immunophenotypic recovery of B-cell subsets in a patient with refractory Class IV LN who achieved durable remission. A 20-year-old woman presented in 2019 edema, nephrotic proteinuria (8.1 g/day), hematuria, hypoalbuminemia, anemia, and acute kidney injury. Laboratory investigations revealed an antinuclear antibody (ANA) titer >1:1,280, anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies of 2,525 IU/mL, and hypocomplementemia. Renal biopsy confirmed Class IV lupus nephritis with diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis and a full-house immunofluorescence pattern. Treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone, RTX, hydroxychloroquine, and immunosuppressive therapy resulted in complete depletion of CD19 + B cells (46.83% to 0%), accompanied by marked reductions in anti-dsDNA antibody levels and improvement in renal function. During seven years of follow-up, CD19 + B cells gradually reconstituted to approximately 20%; however, sustained clinical remission was maintained, with stable renal function, persistently low anti-dsDNA antibody levels, normalization of complement levels, no renal flare, and progressive decline of Antinuclear antibody (ANA) titers to 1:40 and became undetectable. The case demonstrates a persistent dissociation between peripheral CD19 + B-cell repopulation and renal disease activity in vivo . The findings suggest that the quality of immune reconstitution, rather than the absolute number of CD19 + B cells, may be associated with sustained remission after RTX therapy and support the potential value of longitudinal immunophenotypic monitoring.

items.title: Implementing Routine Mental Health Screening and Structured Follow-up for Youth With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A Single-center Quality Improvement Project.
items.abstract: Youth with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) have higher rates of anxiety and depression, yet pediatric rheumatology clinics rarely embed systematic mental health care into routine care. Unrecognized symptoms can impair physical functioning and disease management. The objectives of this quality improvement initiative were to increase (1) anxiety/depression screening from 0% to ≥75% and (2) algorithm-concordant follow-up for youth screening positive from 0% to ≥75%. Our team implemented iterative plan-do-study-act cycles in a pediatric rheumatology clinic at McMaster Children's Hospital. A key driver diagram and fishbone analysis informed interventions, including workflow redesign, staff training, electronic medical record supports, and a standardized follow-up algorithm. We screened youth with JIA 12-18 years of age using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4), an ultra-brief self-report tool used to detect anxiety and depression. Process measures included the percentage of eligible visits with PHQ-4 screening completed and the percentage of screened visits with documented algorithm-concordant follow-up. Outcome measures captured screening results while balancing measures assessed patient and healthcare provider acceptability. PHQ-4 screening increased from 0% to sustained percentages of ≥75% across 266 audited visits (May 2024-August 2025). Overall, 17% of youth screened positive (PHQ-4 ≥ 3). After implementing the follow-up algorithm, ≥75% of screened visits documented education, referral, and/or safety planning. Screening was acceptable to patients and health care providers, with no reported workflow disruption. Embedding PHQ-4 screening with a structured follow-up pathway is feasible and sustainable in a pediatric rheumatology clinic, supporting timely and equitable identification of mental health needs and advancing integrated biopsychosocial care for youth with JIA.

items.title: Anomalous systemic arterial supply to the basal segment of the left lung with large vessel giant cell arteritis demonstrated by 18F-FDG PET/CT.
items.abstract: We report a rare case of anomalous systemic arterial supply to the basal segment of the left lung (ABLL) coexisting with large-vessel giant cell arteritis (LV-GCA) in a 73-year-old woman. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) demonstrated inflammatory involvement of both the aorta and the anomalous artery. To reduce vascular and perioperative risks, immunosuppressive therapy was initiated first, resulting in improvement in clinical and radiological findings. This case highlights the importance of controlling active vasculitis before definitive surgical treatment.

items.title: Long-term evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for systemic sclerosis (NISSC1-LTE): a cohort study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis is a rare and heterogeneous chronic autoimmune disease. It has the highest mortality of the rheumatic diseases and few treatment options exist. Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) is an effective and established therapeutic option in selected patients with early severe systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis in real-life clinical practice. This cohort study (NISSC1-LTE) followed up patients with systemic sclerosis included in the prospective European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation NISSC1 study who had undergone their first autologous HSCT for severe progressive systemic sclerosis. Follow-up data were collected from 13 participating centres in France, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and Brazil. Participating centres completed a yearly case report form for each patient alive after 2 years and up to 10 years after autologous HSCT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as survival from baseline without evidence of systemic sclerosis progression. Late complications after autologous HSCT, including malignancies, secondary autoimmune diseases, infections, and major adverse cardiovascular events were also analysed. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were involved in the design and conduct of this study. The NISSC1 study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02516124) and is complete. All 80 patients with systemic sclerosis who had an autologous HSCT between Dec 4, 2012, and Jan 19, 2016, were included in this long-term extension study. 12 patients were lost to follow-up, including five patients with a follow-up less than 5 years. Median age at autologous HSCT was 43 years (IQR 33-51), 57 (71%) of 80 patients were female, 23 (29%) were male, and median follow-up was 9·2 years (IQR 8·9-9·6) after autologous HSCT. Progression-free survival was 81% (95% CI 71-88) at 2 years, 72% (61-81) at 5 years, and 60% (47-71) at 10 years. 18 patients died during the study; causes of death were autologous HSCT-related in five (6%) of 80 patients, disease progression in nine (11%) patients, post-autologous HSCT malignancy in two (3%) patients, and late serious infection in two (3%) patients. 34 (43%) of 80 patients maintained remission without immunosuppressive treatment over 10 years. This study provides long-term follow-up data after autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis allowing robust assessment of response rate, late complications, and sustained treatment benefit. The extended timeframe might serve as an important comparator for all upcoming, cellular treatment options. None.

items.title: Performance of the systemic lupus erythematosus disease activity score (SLE-DAS) in daily clinical practice: A prospective study of 125 patients in India.
items.abstract: BackgroundAccurate measurement of disease activity is a cornerstone in the management of patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), to assist in guiding therapeutic decisions. SLE-DAS (SLE Disease Activity Score) is designed to improve accuracy and sensitivity to change compared with the standard SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) score.ObjectivesWe aimed to assess the performance of SLE-DAS to identify flare and clinically meaningful improvement (CMI) in real-life SLE patients in India.MethodsProspective observational study at an Indian Rheumatology Clinic included SLE patients meeting 2012 SLICC and/or 2019 ACR/EULAR criteria, followed for 9 months. At baseline and subsequent follow-up, we recorded SLEDAI-2K, SLE-DAS, PGA, LLDAS, DORIS remission, prednisolone dose, and immunosuppressives; SELENA-SLEDAI flare index (SFI) was evaluated at follow-up. We assessed Spearman correlation, agreement, and discrepancies between SLEDAI and SLE-DAS for flare and improvement detection using an agreement matrix.ResultsA strong correlation was observed between SLEDAI-2K and SLE-DAS (rho = 0.954, 95% CI 0.934-0.968, p < 0.001). SLE-DAS identified CMI in 42.0% of visits compared to 34.8% by SLEDAI-2K. Flare detection sensitivity was higher for SLE-DAS (96%) than SLEDAI-2K (84%), with similar specificity (98.9%). The agreement of SLEDAS remission and low disease activity (LDA) with DORIS remission and LLDAS, respectively, was perfect (κ = 1, p < 0.001). Discordant analysis revealed that SLEDAI-2K underestimated severe flares and missed manifestations such as pneumonitis, AIHA, and serositis.ConclusionSLE-DAS demonstrated superior sensitivity, granularity, and remission alignment compared to SLEDAI-2K, supporting its adoption as a primary clinical index in diverse real-world lupus practices.

items.title: Low-level proteinuria at the initial diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus significantly increases the risk of developing proteinuria-predominant lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: A proportion of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) present with subclinical low-level proteinuria at initial diagnosis that does not meet the formal classification criteria for lupus nephritis (LN). This study aimed to investigate the association between low-level proteinuria at SLE onset and the risk of developing proteinuria-predominant LN. This was a retrospective cohort study using medical records of patients newly diagnosed with SLE from Fujian Medical University Union Hospital between December and March. Inclusion required urine dipstick proteinuria ≤2+; if quantified, protein excretion <500 mg/24h (by the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio [UPCR] or 24-hour proteinuria). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected at the time of initial diagnosis, as well as urinalysis, urine sediment, UPCR, and 24-hour proteinuria during follow-up, where available. The association between various baseline variables and the subsequent development of proteinuria-predominant LN was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model. Of 330 patients screened, 297 were eligible for inclusion in the final analysis, of whom 85 patients had low-level proteinuria at the initial diagnosis. According to multivariable-adjusted models, low-level proteinuria significantly increased the risk of proteinuria-predominant LN (P < 0.001, hazard ratio[HR] = 3.355, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.6646.765), as did male sex (P = 0.001, HR = 3.178, 95% CI: 1.563-6.460). This study highlights that SLE patients with low-level proteinuria at initial diagnosis may require enhanced monitoring for LN, enabling early detection. Future studies are needed to determine the necessity of early intervention.

items.title: Transcriptomic age acceleration is associated with plasmablast-related immune remodeling in IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: Biological aging profoundly influences immune function, yet its role in shaping immune remodeling within chronically inflamed tissues remains unclear. We investigated whether transcriptomic age identifies a plasmablast-associated immune aging pattern in IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). To address this question, bulk RNA sequencing was performed on submandibular gland lesions from 49 patients with IgG4-RD and 3 controls. Transcriptomic age (tAge) was estimated using a transcriptome-based aging model, and age acceleration was calculated as the residual from chronological age. Associations between age acceleration, immune transcriptional modules, and clinical characteristics were evaluated using Spearman correlation analyses. Transcriptomic age correlated with chronological age (ρ = 0.473, P< 0.001), whereas age acceleration was associated with serum IgG4 concentrations (ρ = 0.446, P = 0.001). Among immune transcriptional modules, the plasmablast signature showed the strongest positive association with age acceleration (ρ = 0.312, nominal P = 0.029), although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons (FDR-adjusted P = 0.304). Germinal center B-cell and activated B-cell programs showed inverse trends. The plasmablast module also correlated with serum IgG4 levels. Together, these exploratory findings suggest a coordinated pattern linking transcriptomic age acceleration, plasmablast enrichment, and enhanced IgG4 responses. Rather than establishing a mechanistic pathway, these findings identify a candidate plasmablast-associated immune aging pattern that warrants validation in independent cohorts.

items.title: Machine learning improves 10-year prediction of atherosclerotic plaque progression and cardiovascular events in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: To evaluate the performance of generic and disease-adapted tools in predicting 10-year cardiovascular disease (CVD) events and atherosclerotic plaque progression risk in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and develop a machine learning-based model to improve cardiovascular risk stratification. In a prospective 10-year follow-up carotid and femoral ultrasound study of patients with SLE without prior CVD events, we assessed the performance of 11 CVD risk scores (7 conventional, 4 SLE-adapted) to predict atherosclerotic plaque progression and incident CVD events. We used discrimination (sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve [AUC], Youden index), calibration (Brier Score [BS]) and classification (Matthews correlation coefficient, F1 score) metrics, and logistic regression and time-to-event analyses. A machine learning-based gradient boosting model was developed and internally validated. Among 111 patients (91% female, median age: 43.0 years) with 10-year ultrasonography follow-up, 53 (47.7%) developed new plaques, and 8 (7.2%) had incident CVD events. All scores demonstrated suboptimal performance; sensitivity: 0.00-0.44, AUC 0.58-0.79, and BS: 0.44-0.71. In multivariable analysis, QRISK3 was the only tool independently associated with CVD events and/or plaque progression (HR:1.87, p = 0.027). A machine learning-based score that integrates QRISK3 with disease-related risk factors (disease duration, cumulative glucocorticoid dose, DORIS achievement, antiphospholipid antibodies, hydroxychloroquine) and additional traditional CVD risk factors (physical activity, waist circumference), demonstrated significantly better performance compared to all evaluated scores. Conventional and SLE-adapted tools underestimate CVD events and atherosclerosis progression risk in SLE. A machine learning-based model incorporating disease-specific and traditional cardiovascular risk factors into QRISK3 improves CVD risk stratification.

items.title: Five items are sufficient to assess rheumatoid arthritis disease activity by patient reported outcome measure: a computer adaptive test simulation study.
items.abstract: Disease Activity (DA) monitoring is a standard of care in RA. Rasch measurement theory analyses of legacy RA DA patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) was used to develop a valid item pool of 12 items, covering five domains: Tenderness and swelling, Disease activity, Pain, Stiffness, and Physical functioning. The aim of this study was to determine whether it could be advantageous to administer these 12 RA DA items via a computer adaptive test (CAT). Simulations were conducted to assess whether the 12 RA items would cover all five domains adequately. Two sets of simulations were run with stopping rules equivalent to Cronbach's α values of 0.70 and 0.85, respectively. Further CAT simulations would have been run, if coverage of the five domains were inadequate, based on the statistical information and measurement range of the items. In both sets of initial simulations, stopping rules were most commonly satisfied after the administration of five items. However, these five items only covered three domains, with the Disease activity domain consistently missed. Two sets of five items were generated, with summary measures (maximum and mean standard error) equivalent to the initial simulations. In the context of the simulations undertaken here, a CAT does not provide any major advantage for the purposes of administering the 12 RA DA items of the item pool in comparison to administering one item from each of the five domains, and administering one item from each of the five domains appears to be sufficient. We therefore propose the development of a brief, simple to administer, and psychometrically evidenced PROM for the assessment of RA DA.

items.title: Human Adipose-Derived Stem Cell Transplantation Reverses Multiorgan Impairment in Mice with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disorder, leading to immune-mediated organ injury. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effect of human adipose-derived stem cell (hADSC) transplantation on multiorgan damage in MRL/lpr mice. Conclusion These results indicate that hADSCs may ameliorate multiorgan damage associated with SLE. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA), interleukin-4 (IL-4), and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels were measured in MRL/lpr mice to evaluate changes in renal function and immune status. The spleen and lymph node indices were calculated. Heart, spleen, lymph node, skin and kidney tissues were stained to visualize pathological changes. Semiquantitative analysis of haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining across multiple organs and Masson staining of kidneys were performed, followed by laser confocal tracing of stem cells. Compared with the model group, the hADSC-treated MRL/lpr group had significantly lower ACR, anti-ds-DNA, IFN-γ, IL-4 levels, spleen and lymph node indices ( p  < .01), and lymph node scores ( p  < .05). hADSC transplantation also improved renal dysfunction and immune function, significantly reducing pathological damage to tissues, including the kidney and heart ( p  < .01) and the spleen and lymph nodes ( p  < .05). Furthermore, hADSC treatment significantly alleviated renal fibrosis ( p  < .01) in MRL/lpr mice. These results indicate that hADSCs may ameliorate multiorgan damage associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

items.title: Clinical features and associated factors for porto-sinusoidal vascular disease in primary Sjögren's disease: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: To characterize primary Sjögren's disease (pSjD) patients with porto-sinusoidal vascular disease (PSVD) and identify associated clinical factors. This retrospective study included 7 biopsy-proven pSjD-PSVD patients and 28 age and sex-matched pSjD controls. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and portal hypertension-related data were collected and compared between the two groups. Univariate logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with PSVD. The pSjD-PSVD group had significantly longer disease duration than controls [59 (36, 180) vs. 15 (12, 69) months, p = 0.031]. All PSVD patients presented with splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia [(88 ± 44.01) vs. (176.21 ± 66.37) × 10⁹/L, p = 0.003], leukopenia [(3.05 ± 1.26) vs. (4.51 ± 1.52) × 10⁹/L, p = 0.024], hypoalbuminemia [(35.37 ± 4.06) vs. (38.86 ± 3.00) g/L, p = 0.015], elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [(32.13 ± 11.64) vs. (22.9 ± 7.75) IU/L, p = 0.016], and elevated serum IgG [1970 (1540, 2460) vs. 1435 (1160, 1977.5) mg/dL; p = 0.027]. Univariate logistic regression identified thrombocytopenia (OR = 3.481, p = 0.003), INR > 1.2 (OR = 3.507, p = 0.003), hypoalbuminemia (OR = 8.000, p = 0.007), elevated AST (OR = 1.106, p = 0.04), elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) (OR = 1.033, p = 0.023), hypokalemia (OR = 2.408, p = 0.003), and elevated IgG (OR = 2.079, p = 0.039) as factors associated with PSVD. Elevated IgG did not retain significance in Firth's penalized likelihood regression (OR 3.35, p = 0.142). This exploratory study characterizes the clinical features of pSjD patients with PSVD. A constellation of associated features-long disease duration, splenomegaly with hypersplenism, hepatic synthetic impairment (hypoalbuminemia, INR prolongation, elevated AST/ALP), hypokalemia, and hypergammaglobulinemia-may aid in early identification of portal hypertension. These preliminary findings require validation in large prospective cohorts. Key Points • pSjD may represent an autoimmune condition associated with PSVD, featuring long disease duration, splenomegaly, and cytopenias. • pSjD-PSVD shows mild synthetic dysfunction and AST-predominant enzyme elevation without cirrhosis. • Elevated IgG, hypokalemia, and UIP may help identify pSjD patients who warrant closer surveillance for portal hypertension.

items.title: Predicting 12-month renal non-response in childhood-onset lupus nephritis: added value of kidney biopsy pathology.
items.abstract: Paediatric-specific models for renal response in childhood-onset lupus nephritis (cLN) are scarce. We developed internally validated models for failure to achieve 12-month complete renal response (CRR) and quantified pathology's incremental value. In a single-centre retrospective cohort of 503 children with cLN, the prespecified primary outcome was stringent CRR at 12 months after induction therapy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision-curve analysis, with bootstrap optimism correction. Within the pathology-model subgroup, the incremental value of biopsy findings was assessed by the paired bootstrap difference in AUC between Model 2 and Model 1-restricted. Subsequent renal flare was examined in a 12-month landmark analysis using restricted mean survival time (RMST). Of 503 children, 295 (58.6%) achieved 12-month CRR. Model 1 yielded an AUC of 0.784 (95% CI, 0.745-0.824). Within the pathology-model subgroup, the AUC was 0.734 (95% CI, 0.682-0.788) for Model 1-restricted and 0.828 (95% CI, 0.786-0.870) for Model 2, with a paired ΔAUC of 0.071 (95% CI, 0.029-0.124). Model 2 also reduced prediction error. In the landmark cohort, CRR was associated with 10.0 additional renal flare-free months over 60 months (95% CI, 7.6-12.7). A paediatric-specific clinical model provided useful risk stratification for failure to achieve 12-month CRR, and kidney biopsy pathology offered consistent incremental predictive value when available. These internally validated models require external validation before clinical use.

items.title: Evaluation of the effect of rituximab on fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis using the Chalder Fatigue Scale.
items.abstract: Fatigue is a frequent extra-articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), with a reported prevalence ranging from 40% to 90%. It affects physical, emotional, and cognitive aspects of daily life and significantly impairs quality of life. Although biologic therapies may improve fatigue, the specific effect of rituximab on this symptom remains insufficiently documented. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of rituximab on fatigue at baseline (M0), 4 months (M4), and 6 months (M6) using the Chalder Fatigue Scale (CFS). This prospective, observational, single-center study included patients fulfilling the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria for RA and treated with rituximab. Rituximab was administered as two intravenous infusions (500 mg or 1000 mg) on day 0 and day 15. Fatigue was assessed at M0, M4, and M6 using the CFS, with a score ≥4 indicating clinically significant fatigue. Clinical and biological data were collected at each visit. Statistical analyses were performed using Jamovi version 2.4.14. Ninety-four patients were included (mean age 57±9 years; 88% female). The median CFS score decreased from 4 [2-6] at M0 to 2 [0-4] at M4 (p<0.001) and remained stable thereafter through M6 (p=0.11 for the M4-M6 comparison). Disease activity improved in parallel, with the Disease Activity Score 28 using C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP) decreasing from 4.7±1.1 at M0 to 2.9±0.9 at M4 and remaining stable at M6. Functional status assessed by Health Assessment Questionnaire also improved significantly. In multivariable analysis, higher M0 DAS28-CRP was associated with a greater reduction in fatigue. Rituximab therapy was associated with a significant improvement in fatigue in patients with RA, parallel to reductions in disease activity and functional disability.

items.title: Triptolide and Celastrol for Rheumatoid Arthritis: Mechanism-Guided Nanoarchitectonics for Delivery Strategies to Enhance Efficacy and Reduce Toxicity.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis remains a leading cause of irreversible joint disability worldwide. Triptolide and celastrol, major bioactive compounds derived from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F. (TwHF) , have substantial therapeutic potential for rheumatoid arthritis. However, poor solubility, low oral bioavailability, narrow therapeutic windows, and dose-limiting systemic toxicity limit their clinical translation. This review integrates the anti-rheumatoid arthritis mechanisms of triptolide and celastrol with recent advances in nanodelivery systems to establish a mechanism-guided framework for nanocarrier design and clinical translation. Triptolide and celastrol exert multifaceted anti-rheumatoid arthritis effects by inhibiting inflammatory signaling pathways, regulating macrophage polarization and T-cell homeostasis, suppressing fibroblast-like synoviocyte proliferation, and protecting bone and cartilage. Diverse nanodelivery platforms-including lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, biomimetic, carrier-free, and hybrid systems-have substantially improved the bioavailability and lesion-targeting capability of triptolide and celastrol, achieving superior anti-inflammatory and joint-protective efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. Mechanism-guided nanodelivery may help translate triptolide and celastrol into safer, targeted rheumatoid arthritis therapies. Realizing this potential requires a shift from material-centric research toward application-oriented development supported by rigorous validation.

items.title: Difficult-to-manage psoriatic arthritis: Prevalence, phenotype, and clinical burden in real-world practice: insights from the SCQM registry.
items.abstract: To apply consensus-based, difficult-to-treat definitions of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) and to investigate the prevalence, demographics, and clinical characteristics of difficult-to-manage (D2M)/complex-to-manage (C2M) and treatment-refractory (TR) PsA. Retrospective analysis of data derived from the prospective, multicentre, longitudinal Swiss registry was conducted. Patients were eligible if they initiated their advanced therapy after inclusion in the registry and had ≥12 months of follow-up. Group for Research and Assessment of Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis (GRAPPA) and European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) definitions were applied to identify cases of C2M/D2M and TR. From 2493 patients, 30.4% / 2.6% fulfilled the GRAPPA criteria for C2M/TR disease, while 17% / 7.3% met the D2M/TR EULAR criteria, respectively. At baseline, C2M/D2M patients were more frequently women (p < 0.001), smokers, had higher body mass index (BMI), and presented more comorbidities. C2M/D2M patients also demonstrated higher inflammatory markers, higher prevalence of enthesitis, more axial involvement, more severe psoriasis, and worse disease activity scores compared with non-C2M/non-D2M patients (p ≤ 0.001). However, there were no significant differences regarding the prevalence of HLA-B27, dactylitis, nail disease, or other extra-musculoskeletal manifestations. Within both criteria, the TR subgroup showed higher BMI, swollen joint counts, and tender entheses. D2M-TR patients showed significant differences regarding the inflammatory markers, quality of life, and disease activity measures, compared to non-TR D2M patients (p < 0.05). Applying the GRAPPA and EULAR definitions in a large real-world cohort identified distinct clinical and inflammatory profiles in the C2M/D2M and TR groups, highlighting the need for phenotype-tailored management strategies.

items.title: Microbiota-host interactions: key mechanisms linking periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Periodontitis is one of the most prevalent chronic inflammatory diseases in the oral cavity, characterized by progressive destruction of periodontal supporting tissues. Its pathogenesis involves complex interactions between the oral microbiota and host immune responses. This condition not only severely impacts oral health but is also closely associated with multiple systemic diseases. In recent years, the link between periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) has garnered increasing attention. This review examines the compositional characteristics of the oral microbiota in patients with SLE and the epidemiological evidence linking periodontitis to SLE. It focuses on how periodontitis may trigger or exacerbate SLE's autoimmune responses through the oral microbiota, via mechanisms such as molecular mimicry, cytokine-mediated immune activation, and microbial translocation, while elucidating the underlying pathophysiological and immunological mechanisms. Furthermore, this paper aims to explore potential prevention and treatment strategies based on oral microbial interventions, to provide novel insights and theoretical foundations for adjunctive therapy and disease management in SLE.

items.title: Advanced drug delivery and PBPK modelling as translational tools for precision therapies in juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
items.abstract: Patients with persistent forms of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) often report limited therapeutic benefit from currently available treatments. Despite substantial advances in the management of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and related disorders over recent decades, treatment strategies for JIA remain insufficiently defined. The application of advanced drug delivery systems holds promise in addressing these limitations by enabling controlled and sustained drug release over extended periods. Other integrative approaches such as novel physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling have demonstrated to be a critical tool in optimizing pharmacotherapy in pediatric populations, particularly by improving dose selection and predicting drug disposition. This review summarizes current disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) for JIA management and critically examines the current, still largely prospective, integration of emerging drug delivery systems with PBPK modelling, highlighting existing translational examples alongside key opportunities and challenges for precision therapies in this field.

items.title: Diminished ovarian reserve in systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical, immunological, viral, and therapeutic determinants in a 24-month prospective study.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) predominantly affects women of reproductive age; however, the impact of the disease, chronic inflammation, and its treatments on ovarian reserve remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve in SLE and to evaluate the longitudinal associations of clinical characteristics, therapeutic exposures, and herpesvirus serologies with Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) levels. This observational prospective monocentric study followed 80 premenopausal women (18-45 years) with SLE for 24 months. Clinical data, treatments, AMH levels, and herpesvirus serologies were collected every 6 months. Patients were stratified by diminished ovarian reserve (AMH <1 ng/mL). Longitudinal AMH trajectories and the impact of covariates were evaluated using repeated-measures analyses and linear mixed-effects models. The cohort exhibited a high prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve (45% of the study population), associated with older age (37 ± 7 vs. 34 ± 7 years, p = 0.041), longer disease duration (14 ± 9 vs. 10 ± 6 years, p = 0.026), higher cumulative damage (p = 0.007), and lupus anticoagulant positivity (14% vs. 39%, p=0.009). Disease activity was comparable across groups. Hydroxychloroquine use was more frequent in women without diminished ovarian reserve (89% vs 69%, p = 0.033). Over 24 months, AMH levels remained stable with no progressive decline. Belimumab exposure did not adversely affect AMH trajectories, and viral serologies showed no direct long-term impact on AMH levels. This prospective longitudinal study highlights that diminished ovarian reserve is common in women with SLE. AMH levels remained stable over 24 months, with no adverse longitudinal association with belimumab exposure. Hydroxychloroquine use was associated with a lower prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve and warrants further investigation. Serial AMH assessment may support personalized reproductive counselling in women with SLE.

items.title: Case Report: A young female with co-morbid SLE and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome carrying IRF5 risk variants.
items.abstract: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a thrombotic microangiopathy and primarily caused by abnormalities in the regulation of the alternative complement pathway, with triggers including infection, pregnancy, surgery and autoimmune disorders like systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This paper presents a case of a 21-year-old female carrying a SLE susceptibility variant (c.-12 + 198G>T) in the IRF5 , who presented with concurrent manifestations of SLE and aHUS following diarrhea. The uniqueness of this case lies in the fact that comprehensive whole-exome sequencing revealed no known pathogenic mutations in complement genes (such as CFH, CFI, C3 , etc.), yet identified two heterozygous variants in IRF5 , a core gene of the interferon pathway (the c.-12 + 198G>T risk variant and the c.179A>G missense variant). Following targeted therapy centered on eculizumab, the patient achieved hematologic remission, but the kidney disease progressed to end-stage renal disease (ESRD), and maintenance hemodialysis was initiated. This case suggests that the genetic susceptibility underlying aHUS occurring in the context of SLE may extend beyond the classical complement pathway, and that excessive activation of the interferon pathway may be a key factor in triggering a complement activation 'storm' that manifests as aHUS. This observation suggests a possible link between IRF5-related interferon signaling and complement-mediated TMA, and highlights the need for further functional studies. It also emphasizes the importance of early recognition of aHUS and initiation of complement-inhibiting therapy in cases of SLE complicated by TMA.

items.title: Decoding molecular heterogeneity in lupus nephritis: integrating single-cell and spatial multi-omics for endotype-driven precision therapeutics.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) develops in 40-60% of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and remains the leading cause of renal morbidity and progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). While the upstream immunological events initiating LN-including loss of self-tolerance, pathogenic autoantibody production, glomerular immune complex deposition, and type I interferon (IFN) activation-are broadly shared, accumulating evidence demonstrates that these convergent triggers give rise to molecularly heterogeneous tissue injury programs at the renal level. This fundamental divergence provides a mechanistic explanation for the inconsistent therapeutic responses observed with standardized immunosuppressive protocols. Advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial gene expression mapping, CITE-seq, and cross-platform multi-omic integration have deconvolved this heterogeneity into at least five recognizable tissue-level injury programs: (i) an IFN-γ-polarized macrophage-tubular epithelial cell co-activation circuit, (ii) a Tfh-B cell ectopic germinal center pathway, (iii) a neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-driven inflammatory cascade, (iv) a podocyte-autonomous injury program, and (v) a TREM2+ macrophage-orchestrated fibrotic program. Concurrently, multiplexed urinary biomarker platforms are under development as non-invasive surrogates for tissue-level pathogenic activity. This review synthesizes current understanding of disease mechanisms, molecular profiling evidence, biomarker candidates, and mechanism-directed therapies corresponding to each tissue injury program. We map existing and investigational agents-including anifrolumab, obinutuzumab, voclosporin, CAR-T cell therapy, and complement inhibitors-to their mechanistic targets and delineate the design requirements for prospective biomarker-stratified trials essential to validating molecularly guided treatment selection.

items.title: Alopecia areata coexisting with Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Sjögren's syndrome: case report of hair regrowth and selected laboratory changes during combination treatment including tofacitinib.
items.abstract: Alopecia areata (AA) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by transient, non-scarring hair loss and preservation of the hair follicle. Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) and Sjögren's syndrome (SS) are common systemic autoimmune disorders that may share genetic and immunological predispositions with AA. Co-occurrence of all three conditions is rarely reported. We report a 36-year-old female who presented with a 1-year history of progressive hair loss involving the occipital scalp margins, with a Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score of 30 at treatment initiation (retrospectively revised to 15 on unblinded image review). She had a 10-year history of HT on stable levothyroxine replacement and a 6-month history of SS. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated TSH (6.299 uIU/mL), markedly elevated TPO-Ab (922.7 IU/mL), positive anti-SSA antibodies. The patient received tofacitinib 5 mg twice daily, together with intralesional compound betamethasone, topical clobetasol propionate, and topical minoxidil. At 6 months, SALT score was 0; TPO-Ab was 255 IU/mL and Tg-Ab was 430 IU/mL; anti-SSA antibodies were negative; and TSH was 2.760 uIU/mL during continued levothyroxine replacement. Baseline and follow-up thyroid assays used different platforms (CLIA vs ECLIA), and the 6-month Tg-Ab value (430 IU/mL) was numerically higher than baseline (307.52 IU/mL); therefore, neither a biological increase nor decrease in thyroid autoantibodies can be confidently inferred from these numbers alone. Hair regrowth occurred under combination treatment and cannot be attributed to tofacitinib alone. No adverse events were reported during the available follow-up (6 months in clinic; 9 months by telephone). This case describes hair regrowth and selected laboratory changes observed during combination treatment including tofacitinib in a patient with AA and comorbid HT/SS. The observations are hypothesis-generating and temporal association does not establish treatment causation.

items.title: Localized lymphoid hyperplasia with prominent IgG4-positive plasma cells in the inferior turbinate mimicking IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: Localized lymphoid masses of the inferior turbinate with prominent IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration are occasionally encountered in clinical practice, yet their nature and relationship to IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) remain uncertain. This study aimed to characterize the clinical, histopathological, and therapeutic features of these lesions. We retrospectively reviewed patients presenting with localized submucosal masses of the inferior turbinate identified on nasal endoscopy at Seoul National University Hospital between January 2020 and May 2023. Biopsies were performed in cases with mucosal disruption, including crusting or bleeding. Classification of IgG4-RD was based on the 2019 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism criteria. The 2011 Comprehensive diagnosis criteria were applied to the patients with available biopsies. Of 14,103 patients undergoing nasal endoscopy, 41 (0.3%) demonstrated localized inferior turbinate submucosal lesions. Eighteen patients underwent biopsy, all of which revealed dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with variable IgG4-positive plasma cell counts. An IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio exceeding 40% was observed in 10 cases (55.6%). However, characteristic histopathological features of IgG4-RD, including storiform fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis, were absent. Only two patients fulfilled the 2019 classification criteria for IgG4-RD, both of whom had extra-nasal involvement. According to the 2011 Comprehensive diagnosis criteria, 2 patients were classified as definite IgG4-RD. Spontaneous improvement during observation occurred in a minority of patients. Surgical treatment resulted in durable symptom control with minimal recurrence, whereas corticosteroid therapy showed variable effectiveness. Localized IgG4-rich lymphoid hyperplasia of the inferior turbinate may represent a distinct benign inflammatory lesion, mimicking a sinonasal manifestation of IgG4-RD. Further studies are required to clarify its pathophysiology, optimal management, and long-term outcomes.

items.title: Macrophage lipid metabolism and inflammasome activation in rheumatoid arthritis: emerging mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and bone erosion. Within the multicellular RA synovial network, macrophages act as important inflammatory effectors and metabolic sensors whose functional states are shaped by lipid metabolic reprogramming. In RA synovium, impaired cholesterol efflux and altered fatty acid flux remodel membrane lipid composition and lipid-raft-dependent Toll-like receptor (TLR)-NF-κB signaling, thereby enhancing the expression of NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) and pro-interleukin-1β (pro-IL-1β). Cholesterol overload or crystallization, saturated fatty acid-induced lipotoxicity, mitochondrial and lysosomal injury, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, ionic imbalance, and lipid peroxidation generate activation-associated signals that lower the threshold for NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Mechanistic studies, largely outside RA, suggest that fatty acid synthase (FASN)-dependent production of palmitate-derived acyl donors may support ZDHHC-mediated NLRP3 palmitoylation, subcellular trafficking, NEK7 interaction, ASC recruitment, and inflammasome assembly. Liver X receptor (LXR) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) function as complementary lipid-sensing regulators: LXR mainly controls cholesterol efflux and membrane signaling, whereas PPARs coordinate fatty acid handling, mitochondrial adaptation, efferocytosis, and resolution-associated programs. Activation of the NLRP3-caspase-1 axis promotes IL-1β and IL-18 maturation and gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis, amplifying macrophage-fibroblast-like synoviocyte crosstalk, immune-cell recruitment, osteoclastogenesis, and structural joint damage. Because direct validation of the complete FASN-palmitoylation-NLRP3 sequence in RA synovial macrophages remains limited, this axis is presented as a testable RA-relevant mechanistic framework rather than an established RA-specific pathway while highlighting potential targets for macrophage-directed immunometabolic intervention.

items.title: Gut microbiota and intestinal permeability in rheumatoid arthritis: therapeutic implications and future directions.
items.abstract: Interactions between the intestinal microbiota, epithelial barrier and mucosal immune system have prompted investigation of gut-directed interventions in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This review examines whether modifying these interactions can improve clinical outcomes and assesses the strength of the available evidence in RA. In experimental arthritis, interventions that preserve epithelial integrity or alter microbial metabolism can reduce disease severity, providing a biological basis for further study. However, their relevance to human RA remains uncertain, since effects observed in animal models do not establish clinical efficacy, and changes in intestinal measurements alone do not demonstrate improvement in joint disease. Future controlled trials should assess disease activity, and physical function alongside microbial composition and function, intestinal measurements and immune responses. Repeated sampling may help establish whether intestinal changes precede or accompany clinical improvement, while recording medication exposure and dietary intake is needed to interpret these relationships. Candidate biomarkers will require prospective validation before they can be used to select patients for treatment. These studies should determine whether gut-directed interventions provide additional clinical benefit, in whom, and at what risk.

items.title: The correlation between epicardial adipose tissue thickness and left ventricular systolic function in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can cause myocardial damage and left ventricular dysfunction in patients. Abnormal deposition of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) can promote the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to investigate changes in EAT thickness in patients with SLE and apply two-dimensional speckle tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) to study the correlation between EAT and left ventricular systolic function. This case-control study recruited a total of 67 SLE patients as the case group and 31 healthy individuals as the control group. Left ventricular systolic function parameters were measured using 2D-STE. Changes and correlations in laboratory indicators, EAT, and left ventricular systolic function parameters were compared between groups. Compared with the control group, the case group showed significantly increased EAT and diastolic left ventricular posterior wall thickness (LVPWD) ( P <0.05). High-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (AP2C LS), apical three-chamber longitudinal strain (AP3C LS), apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (AP4C LS), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were significantly reduced ( P  < 0.05). The 18-segment left ventricular longitudinal strain was further grouped according to coronary artery supply; the LAD, RCA, and LCX groups in the patient cohort all showed reductions compared with the healthy control group ( P  < 0.05). Spearman correlation analysis revealed that EAT was negatively correlated with GLS ( r  = -0.39, P  < 0.05), LAD group ( r  = -0.26, P  < 0.05), RCA group ( r  = -0.47, P  < 0.05), and LCX group ( r  = -0.29, P  < 0.05), and positively correlated with duration of illness (DT) ( r  = 0.41, P  < 0.05) and age ( r  = 0.45, P  < 0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis confirmed that EAT is an important influencing factor of left ventricular longitudinal strain function ( P  < 0.05). Increased epicardial adipose tissue thickness is negatively correlated with left ventricular systolic function. EAT can effectively reflect changes in left ventricular systolic function in SLE patients, providing a basis for clinical management and early intervention.

items.title: The prediagnostic period of Behçet's disease: a nationwide population-based study.
items.abstract: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD. We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched case-control study using the electronic health records of Leumit Health Services. Patients with BD fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease or International Study Group classification criteria were identified by manual chart review and matched 1:5 with controls by sex, age, socioeconomic category and year of first observation. Clinical diagnoses, diagnostic investigations and laboratory measurements and medication dispensing recorded during the five years preceding diagnosis were compared between groups. Early and late laboratory measurements within the prediagnostic period were analyzed to assess temporal trends. Manifestations documented over the entire available record were analyzed separately. The study included 218 patients who subsequently developed BD and 1,090 matched controls. During the five years preceding diagnosis, future patients with BD more frequently exhibited oral aphthosis (36.2% vs 3.0%; OR 18.2), panuveitis (4.6% vs 0.1%; OR 52.4), inflammatory polyarthritis (7.3% vs 0.6%; OR 14.3), and venous thromboembolism (4.6% vs 0.2%; OR 26.2) (all P<0.001). Over the entire available record, oral aphthosis was documented in 61.0% of patients with BD and 11.8% of controls. Autoimmune serology was frequently requested but remained largely negative. Laboratory analyses demonstrated a biphasic trajectory. Absolute monocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were lower than in controls at the early assessment (0.40 vs 0.44 ×10 9 /L, P = 0.009, and 1.45 vs 1.49, P = 0.023) but significantly higher near diagnosis (0.64 vs 0.58 ×10 9 /L, P = 0.025, and 2.44 vs 2.09, P = 0.003). This transition was accompanied by rising CRP, ESR, platelet count and globulin levels, persistently lower mean corpuscular volume and consistently higher IgA at both assessments (247 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.009, and 256 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.012), whereas IgG and IgM remained comparable between groups. BD seems to be preceded by a clinically and biologically active prediagnostic phase characterized by a distinct inflammatory multisystem footprint.

items.title: Effectiveness and safety of bee venom pharmacopuncture for rheumatoid arthritis-related pain and disease activity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by joint pain, inflammation, and progressive joint destruction. Bee venom (BV) pharmacopuncture has been used in East Asia for RA, but its clinical effectiveness and safety remains uncertain. We evaluated BV pharmacopuncture for pain, disease activity, treatment response, and adverse events (AEs) in patients with RA. We systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, SciELO, CNKI, CiNii, KISS, and other regional databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, meta-analyses were conducted using RevMan 5.4, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Seventeen RCTs involving 1,304 patients with RA were included, and 14 contributed to meta-analysis. Compared with Western medicine, BV significantly improved pain-related outcomes as monotherapy (standardized mean difference [SMD] -0.99, 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.37 to -0.60; I 2  = 20%) and add-on therapy (SMD -1.14, 95% CI -2.11 to -0.17; I 2  = 93%). Only one study evaluated disease activity using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on the erythrocyte sedimentation rate and reported a significant benefit with BV. Although most other disease activity-related outcomes favored BV, the overall effect remained uncertain because the evidence was limited and heterogeneous. BV improved the response rate, defined as a ≥ 30% improvement, as add-on therapy (risk ratio [RR] 1.18, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.36; I 2  = 9%), but not in direct comparisons with Western medicine (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.16; I 2  = 0%; p  = 0.06). The risk of AEs was relatively low with BV monotherapy (risk difference [RD] -0.17, 95% CI -0.34 to -0.01; I 2  = 37%) and add-on comparisons (RD = -0.16, 95% CI -0.26 to -0.06; I 2  = 0%). No serious BV-related AEs, including anaphylaxis, were reported. BV pharmacopuncture may improve pain and treatment response in RA without increasing the risk of AEs. However, these findings are supported by low certainty of evidence, and the effect on disease activity remains uncertain. Further high-quality RCTs with standardized treatment protocols and validated outcome measures are warranted to establish its clinical efficacy and safety. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42021238058, PROSPERO CRD42021238058.

items.title: Telitacicept for the treatment of Sjögren's disease complicated by unilateral vocal fold immobility, severe hypergammaglobulinemia, and diabetes: a case report.
items.abstract: Sjögren's Disease (SjD) involves diverse extraglandular manifestations (EGMs). Severe hypergammaglobulinemia and suspected recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) -related unilateral vocal fold immobility represent aggressive phenotypes. Management of such presentations may be constrained by metabolic comorbidities such as diabetes, which limit the use of conventional high-dose glucocorticoids. Herein, we describe a 48-year-old female with SjD and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) who presented with severe hypergammaglobulinemia (IgG 38.9 g/L), acute hoarseness, and sicca symptoms. Laryngostroboscopy demonstrated left-sided unilateral vocal fold immobility, possibly suggestive of neurogenic paralysis. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) did not identify obvious masses or extrinsic compression along the visualized RLN course, reducing the likelihood of a compressive or malignant etiology. The EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) score was 26. A combined therapeutic regimen comprising telitacicept (160 mg/week), methylprednisolone (20 mg/day) and hydroxychloroquine (0.2 g, twice daily) was initiated, both to minimize glucocorticoid exposure and to target the patient's profound B-cell hyperactivity manifested by severe hypergammaglobulinemia. Marked serological and symptomatic improvements were observed during treatment. Within 15 weeks, the IgG level decreased to 14.6 g/L, rheumatoid factor (RF) decreased from 759 IU/mL to 58.3 IU/mL, and the ESSDAI score dropped to 6. The patient experienced symptomatic improvement of hoarseness, while methylprednisolone was successfully tapered to 4 mg/day. Clinical stability based on patient-reported symptoms persisted through the 12-month follow-up. This case is hypothesis-generating: A telitacicept-containing regimen may produce marked serological improvement and symptomatic benefit for high-activity SjD with laryngeal/vocal fold involvement, while reducing glucocorticoid-related metabolic risks. Definitive efficacy requires confirmation in larger controlled studies.

items.title: Tophaceous gout-related carpal tunnel syndrome and flexor tendon involvement: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Tophaceous gout is an uncommon but clinically important cause of secondary carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS), with lesions ranging from diffuse flexor tenosynovitis to intratendinous destruction and direct median nerve involvement. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched through 23 July 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar, publisher-page verification, and citation searching. Human primary reports explicitly attributing CTS or wrist-level median neuropathy to gout, tophus, or monosodium urate deposition were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened records. Fifty-seven reports (27 complete/detailed and 30 limited clinical sources) formed the primary synthesis and underwent design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal; 12 bibliographic or translation-limited reports were retained as historical ancillary evidence. Primary reports were additionally classified post hoc by causal certainty. Of 478 database records, 302 unique records were screened, and 69 canonical reports were included. The 57-report primary synthesis comprised 44 case reports or clinical-image reports, 12 case series, and one nonrandomized comparative study, representing at least 120 patients, 152 CTS wrists, and 146 gout-attributable wrists. Sex was reportable for 117 patients, of whom 111 (94.9%) were male. Causal certainty was Tier 1 (direct local confirmation) in 41 reports, Tier 2 (anatomically supported) in 5, and Tier 3 (explicit report-level attribution) in 11. Post hoc sensitivity analyses retaining Tier 1 + 2 ( n  = 46) and then Tier 1 only ( n  = 41) did not change the principal qualitative interpretations. Open decompression with lesion treatment was the most frequently reported operative pattern, but evidence remained insufficient to determine a preferred tendon procedure. JBI findings are reported by design; 481 item-level judgments are retained only as an audit total. Gout should be considered in atypical, acute, severe, recurrent, bilateral, or mass-associated CTS. In surgically treated reports, decompression was commonly combined with individualized management of tophaceous and tendon disease. The evidence is predominantly case-based and hypothesis-generating and is insufficient to define a validated treatment pathway or preferred tendon procedure.

items.title: Exploring the faecal miRNA profile in familial Mediterranean fever patients and the role of miR-21-5p in inflammatory pathways associated with FMF pathogenesis.
items.abstract: Beyond MEFV mutations, epigenetics seems to play an important role in the manifestation of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). This study aimed to evaluate the differential expression of selected miRNAs in stool samples from FMF patients, and to investigate the functional role of miR-21-5p in FMF-related inflammatory pathways. Thirty-four FMF patients, 15 patients with Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI), and 25 healthy controls were enrolled in this study. The faecal levels of 27 miRNAs associated with inflammation, apoptosis, and autophagy were quantified by qRT-PCR. The functional role of miR-21-5p in regulating NF-ĸB and pyrin inflammasome pathways was investigated in LPS-stimulated THP-1 derived macrophages transfected with an anti-mir-21-5p inhibitor via western blot. Among the 27 analysed miRNAs, eight were significantly upregulated in FMF patients compared with controls, with miR-21-5p, miR-30e-3p, and miR-148a-3p uniquely elevated in FMF. Downregulation of the anti-inflammatory miR-186-5p and miR-374b-5p was observed particularly in M694V homozygous patients, while let-7d-5p, and miR-148b-3p were associated with higher disease severity. Functional inhibition of miR-21-5p in LPS-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages reduced NF-ĸB activation and decreased the expression of inflammasome-associated proteins except ASC, consistent with ASC-independent modulation of inflammasome signalling, potentially through direct caspase-1 activation. Our findings highlight the role of miRNAs in intestinal inflammation and their potential as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers in FMF. Our functional data underscore the regulatory role of miR-21-5p in FMF-related inflammatory pathways and warrant further studies to elucidate its therapeutic potential, particularly in patients refractory to colchicine or as an adjunct to existing treatments.

items.title: Invisible neuropsychiatric burden in Behçet's disease without central nervous system involvement: a phenotype-based comparison.
items.abstract: Neuro-Behçet's disease (NBD) is a serious complication of Behçet's disease (BD); however, data focusing on neuropsyhiatric symptoms in patients without overt neurological involvement remain limited. The burden of neuropsychiatric symptoms in non-neuro-Behçet's disease (non-NBD) across different BD phenotypes were evaluated. In this cross-sectional, single-centre study, 152 patients with BD were classified as mucocutaneous (mBD, n=69), ocular (oBD, n=26), vascular (vBD, n=40), or NBD (n=17); and familial mediterranean fever (FMF) patients (n=37) for autoinflammatory burden and colchicine exposure and healthy controls (HC, n=29) were included. Neuropsychiatric assessment included headache characteristics, Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Any headache was reported in 72.5% of mBD, 69.2% of oBD, and 67.5% of vBD patients, compared with 52.9% in NBD, 64.9% in FMF, and 41.4% in HC (p=0.012). Migraine-type headache was the most frequent subtype across groups. BAI scores did not differ significantly but tended to be higher in mBD. In contrast, depressive symptoms differed significantly (p=0.005), with higher BDI scores in mBD (14) and vBD (13.5) compared with NBD (11), FMF (9) and HC (7). Cognitive impairment (MMSE ≤23) was more frequent in mBD (41.2%) and NBD (41.2%) than in vBD (15.0%), FMF (10.8%) and HC (24.1%) (p=0.001). Neuropsychiatric manifestations represent a substantial burden in BD even in the absence of overt neurological involvement, particularly in mBD with less control of inflammation and regular follow-up. These findings support the need for routine neuropsychiatric evaluation across all BD phenotypes, extending beyond the traditional NBD framework.

items.title: Serum ferritin predicts response to tocilizumab in glucocorticoid-resistant adult-onset Still's disease: a prospective real-world cohort study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of tocilizumab (TCZ) in glucocorticoid (GC)-resistant adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and explore predictors of clinical response. This prospective, single-centre cohort study enrolled consecutive eligible patients with GC-resistant AOSD who initiated intravenous TCZ (4-8 mg/kg every four weeks) between June 2021 and June 2024. The primary outcome was clinical remission at 12 months per 2024 EULAR/PReS criteria (clinically inactive disease [CID] lasting ≥6 months). Secondary outcomes included CID rate at 6 months, laboratory and clinical activity scores, GC dose reduction, TCZ retention, and safety. Forty patients (median age 35.5 years; 80% female) were included. Clinical remission at 12 months was 55.0% (22/40); CID at 6 months was 62.5% (25/40). Significant improvements were observed in C-reactive protein (CRP), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), serum ferritin (SF), and Pouchot scores (all p<0.001). Median daily prednisone dose decreased by 91%, from 50.0 mg to 4.4 mg (p<0.001). Baseline SF levels ≥ 2500 μg/L were independently associated with lower remission rates (adjusted odds ratio 0.19, 95% CI 0.04 - 0.94; p=0.042) and higher GC requirements at 12 months (β=5.55, 95% CI 1.16 - 9.94; p=0.015). The 12-month TCZ retention rate was 65.0%. Serious adverse events included macrophage activation syndrome (MAS, 7.5%) and lymphoma (2.5%). TCZ is effective and steroid-sparing in GC-resistant AOSD. Baseline hyperferritinaemia (SF ≥2500 μg/L) is a potential biomarker for poorer outcomes, suggesting a need for tailored management.

items.title: Left ventricular assessment using speckle-tracking echocardiography in Behçet's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory disorder associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity. Conventional echocardiography often fails to detect early myocardial involvement. Speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) allows sensitive assessment of left ventricular (LV) myocardial deformation, particularly global longitudinal strain (GLS). The aim of this study is to systematically evaluate LV systolic function assessed by STE in BD patients and to compare GLS differences with healthy controls. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science databases were searched for studies assessing LV strain by STE in BD. Studies using two- or four-dimensional STE were included. Pooled standardised mean differences (SMD) in LV GLS between BD patients and controls were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochrane Q test and was further explored using Baujat plot and leave-one-out analysis. PROSPERO registry number: CRD420251251109. Eight studies including 373 BD patients and 402 controls were included. LV GLS was not significantly reduced in BD compared to controls (SMD -0.59; 95% CI -1.21 to 0.04; p=0.06). Subgroup analyses showed that GLS impairment was more pronounced in patients with non-active disease (SMD -0.9; 95% CI -1.71 to -0.08), while no significant difference was observed in patients with no cardiovascular risk factors (p=0.20). BD patients do not exhibit consistent subclinical LV systolic dysfunction in strain echocardiography. Further studies are required to optimise the use of STE in this population.

items.title: Behçet's disease and pregnancy: retrospective study and updated review of the literature.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease (BD) is a rare, chronic-relapsing multisystem vasculitis of unknown aetiology, typically presenting with bipolar aphthosis (oral and genital), cutaneous lesions, and ocular involvement. It is most often diagnosed during reproductive age and its coexistence with pregnancy is therefore not uncommon. The interaction between BD and pregnancy is complex and bidirectional: pregnancy can modulate disease activity, while the disease itself may influence maternal, foetal, and neonatal outcomes. Current literature remains limited and frequently yields inconsistent conclusions regarding this relationship. In light of these considerations, this study aims to evaluate the impact of BD on pregnancy outcomes and to characterise the disease course during pregnancy in a cohort of affected patients. We retrospectively analysed data from 25 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of BD and a total of 48 pregnancies, followed at the outpatient clinics of Policlinico Umberto I, Rome, Italy. Clinical records were reviewed and supplemented with telephone interviews to ensure accuracy and completeness of information. Additionally, a literature review wasconducted using major databases such as PubMed, Cochrane and Google Scholar to provide context and comparison with previously published findings. Contrary to the prevailing consensus in the literature, which often reports increased disease activity during pregnancy, our findings indicate that in 80% of cases it remained stable, with no significant differences compared to the pre-pregnancy period. When flares did occur, they primarily involved oral aphthosis, aligning with previously reported patterns. Pregnancy outcomes were generally favourable, with an overall live birth rate of 89.58%. Complications were observed in 13 pregnancies (27.08%), mostly in pregnancies that occurred before BD diagnosis (21%). The most common were spontaneous miscarriage and deep vein thrombosis. Other complications, each occurring in one case, included threatened miscarriage, preterm delivery, low birth weight, gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and premature rupture of membranes. Our findings suggest that Behçet's disease does not usually worsen during pregnancy and that favourable pregnancy outcomes are achievable. Nonetheless, the risk of complications, although relatively low, supports the need for preconception counselling and close multidisciplinary monitoring. This study contributes new insights from a specialised referral centre to the limited body of evidence available on this topic.

items.title: Psoriatic Arthritis Without Cutaneous Manifestations: A Case of Diagnostic Delay, Pathologic Progression, and Psychological Burden.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory musculoskeletal disease. Presentations can vary, but common manifestations include peripheral arthritis, dactylitis, enthesitis, nail changes, and skin changes, including psoriasis. Diagnosis is often challenging due to the absence of specific biomarkers, variable clinical presentation, and overlap with conditions such as osteoarthritis and fibromyalgia. These diagnostic obstacles contribute to frequent misdiagnosis and delay in treatment, which, over time, leads to irreversible joint damage, functional impairment, and increased comorbidities. A 62-year-old woman with a 15-year history of chronic pain attributed to fibromyalgia and osteoarthritis presented to primary care with persistent hand and foot pain and worsening depressive symptoms. Prior treatments failed to provide relief. Imaging and laboratory evaluation were not consistent with her previous diagnoses of fibromyalgia and osteoarthritis. Although she lacked characteristic psoriatic skin lesions, further history revealed a family history of psoriasis in her daughter and grandson. This finding prompted consideration of PsA, and the diagnosis was made based on clinical presentation and history. The patient was started on disease-modifying antirheumatic drug therapy and escitalopram, with significant improvement in both pain and mood within one month. This case exemplifies the impacts of delayed diagnosis in a patient with PsA without cutaneous manifestations. Common misdiagnoses of PsA can include fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, and rheumatoid arthritis due to overlapping subjective and objective findings, making diagnosis difficult. This delay leads to prolonged initiation of treatment and thus results in further joint damage, functional decline, and mental health impacts. Quicker suspicion and thorough history taking in patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain unresponsive to treatment could potentially improve diagnostic delay trends of PsA, even in the absence of cutaneous findings.
